stories.label: Iran-US-Israel war: Gulf states weigh military entry, Hormuz blockade tightens
stories.summary: Gulf states (Saudi, UAE) considering military entry if Iran hits infrastructure. IRGC turned back container ship at Hormuz. Pakistan Sindh province weighing COVID-style lockdowns for fuel conservation.
stories.context:
CONTEXT: Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Gulf

ORIGINS
1953  CIA and MI6 overthrew Prime Minister Mosaddegh, ending Iran's experiment in democratic governance and installing Shah Pahlavi as a US client ruler.
1979  The Iranian Revolution ended the Pahlavi monarchy and established the Islamic Republic under Khomeini, reversing twenty-six years of US-aligned rule.
1980  Iraq invaded Iran, beginning an eight-year war that killed around 500,000 people.
1981  The Gulf Cooperation Council was founded as a Saudi-led bloc of six Gulf states — partly in response to the revolution and the war next door.

THE STRAIT
The Strait of Hormuz is 24 miles wide at its narrowest, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
Iran controls the entire north coast; the UAE and Oman's Musandam exclave share the south.
During the 1980s tanker war, Iraq carried out 283 attacks on merchant vessels passing through these waters, and Iran 168.
In April 1988, the US launched Operation Praying Mantis against Iranian naval targets in retaliation for the mining of a US warship.
The IRGC Navy, a branch of the Revolutionary Guard separate from Iran's regular navy, is the force that patrols these waters today.

THE PROXY WAR
1985  Iran began backing Hezbollah in Lebanon and later Hamas in Palestine, opening a long proxy front against Israel.
2015  The JCPOA nuclear deal was signed with the P5+1, briefly easing tensions over Iran's nuclear program.
2024  The proxy conflict escalated into direct military confrontations between Iran and Israel.
June 2025  Iran and Israel fought a twelve-day war that drew in the United States.

GULF STATES AND THE US
Saudi-US relations were formalized in 1933 and sealed by the 1951 Mutual Defense Agreement: American military protection in exchange for reliable oil supply priced in dollars.
The GCC functions as both an economic union and a military alliance, but its members have never fought a war against a neighboring Muslim state.
Saudi Arabia and the UAE now weigh military entry against Iran if their own infrastructure is struck — a threshold that would shatter decades of Gulf security architecture.

NOW
The IRGC has turned back a container ship at the Strait of Hormuz, testing blockade enforcement in the world's most critical oil chokepoint.
Pakistan's Sindh province is considering COVID-style lockdowns to conserve fuel — a sign that the economic shockwave has already reached South Asia.
Gulf states face the choice their geography has always threatened: between their US security alliance and the certainty that war will be fought on their own soil, against their own neighbors.

---
> **وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَإِن بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن فَاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوا ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ**
> *And if two factions among the believers should fight, then make settlement between the two. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the ordinance of Allah. And if it returns, then make settlement between them in justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.* — Al-Hujurat 49:9
> Ibn Kathir: Allah commands Muslims to make peace between believers who fight each other, citing how Al-Hasan ibn Ali brought reconciliation between the people of Sham and Iraq after tremendous wars — and that both parties retain the name "believers" even in conflict.

stories.label: TSA workers unpaid in second shutdown as ICE militarizes airports
stories.summary: Delta suspends Congress VIP airport services during DHS shutdown. TSA agents working unpaid, long lines at airports. Senate deal reportedly imminent.
stories.context:
CONTEXT: The post-9/11 airport security state and its fractures

ORIGINS
2001  Nineteen hijackers seized four airliners on September 11, crashing them into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and a Pennsylvania field — the attacks that restructured American domestic security.
2001  Congress passed the Aviation and Transportation Security Act, creating the Transportation Security Administration to consolidate air travel security under a single federal agency.
2002  The Homeland Security Act established the Department of Homeland Security and reorganized the federal government, passing the Senate 90–9.
2002  TSA was transferred from the Department of Transportation into the new DHS.
2002  Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created under the same act, absorbing the functions of the Immigration and Naturalization Service and the United States Customs Service.

THE APPARATUS
TSA holds authority over the security of all transportation systems within and connecting to the United States.
ICE's stated mission covers criminal investigations, immigration enforcement, national security, and public safety — a mandate broad enough to operate well beyond borders.
The FAA, a separate agency under the Department of Transportation, regulates civil aviation including air traffic control, personnel certification, and airport standards.
DHS itself is responsible for anti-terrorism, border control, immigration, cybersecurity, transportation security, and maritime security — the largest post-9/11 reorganization of federal power.

SHUTDOWN MECHANICS
A government shutdown occurs when Congress fails to enact funding legislation before the fiscal year begins.
During a shutdown, federal agencies curtail services, cease non-essential operations, and furlough non-essential workers.
Only employees deemed essential — those protecting human life or property — are retained on duty without pay.
TSA screeners, classified as essential, must continue working through shutdowns unpaid.

THE AIRPORT
LaGuardia Airport sits on 680 acres in East Elmhurst, Queens, on the northwestern shore of Long Island bordering Flushing Bay.
The facility was established in 1929 and began operating as a public airport in 1939, named after former New York City mayor Fiorello La Guardia.

WHY IT MATTERS
Aviation safety is the study and practice of managing risks across all aspects of flight, from personnel training to infrastructure design.
Adverse weather, turbulence, icing, and reduced visibility are recognized as major contributing factors to safety outcomes — but so is institutional failure to act on known risks.
The post-9/11 security apparatus was built to prevent catastrophic failure, yet its workforce — the people who physically operate it — can be forced to work without pay whenever Congress stalls on funding.

stories.label: European PMI signals stagflation from Iran war energy shock
stories.summary: UK manufacturers hit by sharpest cost rise since Black Wednesday 1992. Iran war oil shock now measurable in PMI data across industrial economies. Real-economy transmission of Hormuz disruption.
stories.context:
CONTEXT: European stagflation from Iran war energy shock

ORIGINS OF OIL AS WEAPON

1951  Iran nationalised Anglo-Iranian Oil Company assets at Abadan, expelling foreign operators — Britain responded with blockade and covert regime change rather than accept sovereign control over Muslim-world resources.
1973  First worldwide oil crisis saw prices increase 400%, proving that disruption at source could paralyse industrial economies thousands of miles away.
1979  Islamic Revolution overthrew the Shah; the second oil crisis followed, with prices doubling as Iranian output collapsed.
1981-1988  Iran-Iraq tanker war turned the Strait of Hormuz into a combat zone, with 451 attacks on merchant vessels demonstrating the chokepoint's fragility.

THE HORMUZ CHOKEPOINT

The Strait of Hormuz runs roughly 104 miles long and narrows to 24 miles at its tightest passage between Iran and Oman's Musandam Peninsula.
Every previous closure threat — during the tanker war, during US-Iran tensions — sent oil markets into panic pricing.
2026  Iran's closure of the strait has led to oil prices increasing by nearly 30%, making it the first actual sustained disruption of the waterway.

STAGFLATION MECHANICS

1965  British politician Iain Macleod coined "stagflation" to describe the UK's simultaneous inflation and stagnation — a condition orthodox economics said could not happen.
The 1970s oil shocks proved it could: supply-side price surges fed inflation while choking growth and raising unemployment at the same time.
Stagflation defies the Phillips Curve assumption that inflation and unemployment move inversely, leaving central banks with no clean policy lever.

TRANSMISSION TO EUROPE

1992  Black Wednesday forced Britain out of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism on 16 September after a failed defence of sterling — the last time UK manufacturers faced a comparable cost shock.
PMI surveys — monthly private-sector purchasing managers' indexes — are now the earliest real-economy signal of industrial contraction.
UK manufacturing PMI is registering the sharpest input-cost rise since that 1992 crisis, with the Hormuz energy shock now measurable across European industrial economies.

WHY IT MATTERS

Every major oil shock since 1951 has originated in or passed through the Muslim world, yet the populations living beside the infrastructure bear the consequences of the wars fought over it.
The pattern repeats: disruption at Hormuz, price transmission through global energy markets, stagflationary pressure landing on European and Asian manufacturers, and policy responses that treat the symptom — inflation — while the underlying conflict continues.
